 DIST. DHARWAD.

THIS PETITION COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
 THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  CRL.P No. 100371 of 2023  ORDER Heard Sri L.S.Sullad, learned counsel for the petitioner and learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.
Perused the records.

2. The present petition is filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. with the following prayer :-
"To direct the respondent, CID Bengaluru to release the petitioner/accused no.15 on the anticipatory bail in event of his arrest in Hubballi Sub-Urban Police Station Crime No. 0048/2017, u/sec. 406, 420, 465, 471, 467, 468 IPC on the file of Principal Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Hubballi, dist. Dharwad."
3.

The brief facts of the case are as under :-
Sachin s/o Shivaji Patil filed a complaint with Hubballi Sub-Urban Police Station on 26.03.2017 which was registered in Crime No.48/2017 for the offences punishable U/sec.406, 420, 465, 471, 467, 468 IPC.
4.

Gist of the complaint averments reveal that the 1 s t accused by name Jignesh Vyas has formed a company called Jignesh Vyas Home Builders and Developers and wanted to construct the flats and assured the complainant that three flats will be sold at the rate of rupees one crore per flat and if the flats are not constructed in time, the advance amount received for the construction of the flats would be repaid with 18% interest.

entities.text: Jignesh Vyas Home Builders and Developers
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Accordingly, money was received by the accused from the complainant.
However there was a breach of promise to construct the flats as is assured in the year 2014.

In the year 2016, cheques were issued towards the return of the advance amount and the same were dishonoured and therefore, sought for action against Jignesh Vyas and others for the aforesaid offences.
After registering the case, police are investigating the matter.

In the meantime, present petitioner has been shown as accused No.15 and he has approached the District Court for grant of anticipatory bail which was dismissed by order dated 19.01.2023 in Crl.Misc.No.5017/2023 by the learned I Addl.District and Sessions Judge, Dharwad, sitting at Hubballi.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 5. Reiterating the grounds urged in the petition, Sri L.S.Sullad, learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently contended that the petitioner is no way concerned with the alleged fraud or cheating and he has been falsely implicated in the case by the investigation agency though the complaint mentions only against Jignesh Vyash who is the 1 s t accused in the matter.
6. He also contended that the petitioner is a law abiding citizen and he is ready to co-operate with the investigation agency and therefore he may be granted anticipatory bail.

7. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader opposes the bail petition by contending that from the date of registration of the case, petitioner is absconding and he is not available to the investigation agency and therefore investigation has crippled to a considerable extent and sought for rejection of the bail petition.

8. She also contended that magnitude of the fraud is very high and therefore, the custodial interrogation of the present petitioner is utmost necessary for effective investigation and filing appropriate report before the jurisdictional Magistrate and the investigation is also handed over for the CID for effective investigation and sought for dismissal of the petition.
9. Having heard the parties, this Court perused the material on record meticulously.
10. The alleged fraud has taken place between the years 2014-16.
The complaint came to be filed by the complainant only against Jignesh Vyash at the first instance.
Police are investigating the matter and they are unable to apprehend the present petitioner who is shown to be accused No.15 in the incident.

11. Admittedly since the petitioner is not available to the investigation agency effective investigation has not been carried out and no appropriate report is filed by the investigation agency and no appropriate report is filed by the investigation agency.
12. Directing the petitioner to join the investigation and co-operate with the investigation agency and to undergo limited period of custodial interrogation to meet the ends of justice in balancing the right of the petitioner as well as the need of investigation agency.
13.
Accordingly, without expressing further opinion on the merits of the matter, following order is passed.

ORDER The criminal petition is allowed subject to the following conditions:
1. The Petitioner is directed to join the investigation by appearing before the Investigation Officer on 29.05.2023 at 10.00 a.m.
2.

The Investigation Officer is at liberty to take the petitioner to custody and complete the custodial investigation if any, on the same day before 6.00 p.m. and thereafter enlarge the petitioner on bail by taking a bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees one Vivek S/O Ramachandra Dhamanse vs The State Of Karnataka on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186644709/
3 lakh only) with two sureties for the likesum.

sentences.text:
3. The petitioner shall co-operate with the Investigating Agency in furnishing his handwriting, specimen signature, bank account and any other details as would be required by the investigation agency.
4.
The petitioner shall not tamper the prosecution witnesses in any manner.
5. The petitioner shall attend the Court regularly and appear before the Investigation agency as and when directed.

6. The petitioner shall mark his attendance before the Investigating Officer on every third Sunday between 10.00 am and 2.00 pm., till the final report is filed or for a period of six months whichever is earlier.
7.
The petitioner shall not directly or indirectly tamper the prosecution evidence or hamper the investigation process in any manner.
8. The petitioner shall not leave the jurisdiction of Dharwad District without prior permission.
Violation of any one of the conditions would entitle the prosecution to seek for cancellation of the bail.
Ordered accordingly.
